texto: If a verb governs **essere** in prossimo (sono uscito, siamo partiti), it will keep **essere** in trapassato (ero uscito, eravamo partiti), with mandatory gender and number agreement.
If you rule **avere** (ho dorto, abbiamo preparato), you will keep **avere** (avevo dorto, avevamo preparato), with invariable termination in **-o**.

frases.it: Elena, siete partiti presto sabato mattina per la gita?
frases.es: Elena, ¿salisteis temprano el sábado por la mañana para la excursión?
frases.en: Elena, did you leave early on Saturday morning for the tour?

frases.it: Volevamo partire alle sette, ma io non avevo dormito bene durante la notte.
frases.es: Queríamos salir a las siete, pero yo no había dormido bien durante la noche.
frases.en: We wanted to leave at 7: 00, but I hadn't slept well during the night.

frases.it: E a che ora siete usciti di casa alla fine?
frases.es: ¿Y a qué hora salisteis de casa al final?
frases.en: And what time did you get out of the house at the end?

frases.it: Eravamo usciti prima della pioggia, verso le nove. Avevamo preparato gli zaini la sera prima.
frases.es: Habíamos salido antes de la lluvia, hacia las nueve. Habíamos preparado las mochilas la noche anterior.
frases.en: We'd been out before the rain, about nine. We had prepared the backpacks the night before.

bloques.pregunta: Why do you say «non avevo dormito» but «eravamo usciti»?

opciones.explicacion: Each verb consistently maintains its auxiliary at all times.

opciones.texto: Because «uscire» is a transitory verb with direct object.
Because the «dormire» subject is always plural.
opciones.explicacion: The subject in the phrase is singular («io avevo dormito»).

bloques.frase: I ragazzi non avevano fame perché ___ pranzato prima di partire.

opciones.explicacion: «Pranzare» is an activity verb that forms the times composed with «avere».
The verbs of eating or lunch do not match «essere».
It corresponds to «noi» (we), but the subject is «i ragazzi» (they).

opciones.texto: The participle matches the masculine plural with the «noi» subject when using «essere».
opciones.explicacion: With «essere» the termination reflects gender and number (-o, -a, -i, -e).

opciones.texto: The participle remains invariable always at any time composed.
opciones.explicacion: The invariability in -or only operates with the «avere» auxiliary.

opciones.texto: La concordancia se establece con el sustantivo femenino «pioggia».
opciones.explicacion: The participle is in accordance exclusively with the subject of the verb.

bloques.frase: Avevamo preparato gli zaini la sera prima
bloques.traduccion: We had prepared the backpacks the night before.
bloques.explicacion: Trapassate with auxiliary «avere» and invariable participle.

bloques.pregunta: What auxiliary corresponds to the «svegliarsi» reflective verb in trapassate?

opciones.explicacion: All reflexive and reciprocal verbs necessarily choose «essere».
The reflexives never accept «avere» in the Italian standard.
«Stare» does not form perfect times in Italian.

bloques.frase: Luca ed Elena si erano ___ molto presto per evitare il traffico.

opciones.explicacion: Mixed third person plural with «essere» auxiliary: deinence in -i.
It is the form of masculine singular.
It is the form of feminine singular.

bloques.pregunta: What explains this fact in the conversation?
bloques.frase: Non avevo dormito bene durante la notte.

opciones.texto: The reason they delayed the exit to the mountain.
opciones.explicacion: Elena slept bad and that's why they didn't leave at seven.

opciones.texto: The reason they definitely canceled the tour.
opciones.explicacion: They didn't cancel the tour, they only left around nine.

opciones.texto: They preferred to travel at night so they could not find rain.
opciones.explicacion: They left in the morning around 9: 00.

intro: In Italian, each verb strictly retains its own auxiliary (avere or essere) both in the prossimo passage and in the prossimo trapassate and other composite times.
